Claude verified a 1665 math proof faster than any human team ever could
caption:
Claude just converted a 360-year-old mathematical proof into 13 million lines of computer code, completing in weeks what human experts spend years on.

The process is called formalization: you take a written proof and turn it into a form a computer can check line by line, with no room for logical shortcuts or assumptions. Claude did this using a tool that accepts nothing on faith and requires every single step to be airtight.

The mathematician whose theorem was verified died in 1665. The fact that an AI can now do this at scale means centuries of unverified mathematics could be confirmed in a fraction of the time it would take any human team.
